tr.td: Tremor evaluation: head, voice, and hand tremor; tremor rating, reversible causes, and functional impact
Four-week follow-up with movement disorders neurology consultation: diagnosis and choice of treatment
Three-month tremor review after starting propranolol and voice therapy

First-line medicine for limb tremor, chosen with movement disorders neurology: propranolol extended-release 60 mg each morning from the four-week visit; check resting heart rate and seated and standing blood pressure at every visit, ask about wheeze, fatigue, low mood, and lightheadedness, and do not stop it suddenly; primidone, started at 12.5 to 25 mg at bedtime, is held as the alternative or add-on, with checks for sedation, unsteadiness, and falls
Movement disorders neurology consultation to confirm the diagnosis against the MDS consensus classification, choose treatment, and advise on head and voice tremor
Speech-language therapy for voice tremor, and occupational therapy for adaptive aids (weighted utensils, lidded cups, thick-barreled pens)

Monitor at every visit: TETRAS performance and daily-living subscales, spiral drawing and handwriting, heart rate and standing blood pressure on propranolol, side effects, falls, and drugs that worsen tremor; yearly: examination for signs beyond tremor, mood, cognition, and an AGS Beers Criteria medication review. Focused ultrasound thalamotomy or deep brain stimulation is considered only if disabling limb tremor persists after adequate trials of propranolol and primidone
Advance care planning: name a health care agent and record goals of care at the annual wellness visit
Less hand tremor with daily tasks on a well-tolerated medicine, with resting heart rate 55 or above and no lightheadedness, by the three-month review
TETRAS performance subscale fell from 22 to 16 and the activities of daily living subscale from 14 to 9 on propranolol; heart rate 64; no lightheadedness or falls
Complete a course of voice therapy and use the strategies on stage
Six-week course completed; steadier sustained notes with breath support and a slightly higher pitch
Use adaptive aids for eating, drinking, and writing
Occupational therapy evaluation completed after the six-month review; weighted utensils, a lidded travel cup, and a thicker pen in use

list.item: At the first visit: TETRAS performance subscale 22 of 64 and activities of daily living subscale 14 of 48. Side-to-side (no-no) head tremor of moderate amplitude, present when sitting and standing and lessened when the head is supported; wavering pitch on a sustained vowel; postural and kinetic tremor of both hands, right slightly more than left, on finger-to-nose testing and when pouring, which she has noticed for several years; spiral drawing with tremor waves; handwriting legible but shaky. No rest tremor, bradykinesia, rigidity, dystonic posturing, or ataxia; normal tandem gait [S]
Falls: none in the past year; Timed Up and Go 9 seconds [S]

Daily impact: spills when carrying full cups, slow to sign autographs and write letters, and the voice tremor is noticeable on sustained notes on stage; independent in all activities and instrumental activities of daily living [S]
Alert, direct, and quick-witted; speech fluent with a mild tremulous quality on sustained vowels; MoCA 28 of 30 [S]
